function: Learned beam hopping pattern and downlink power allocation per beam for a multi-beam LEO satellite with integrated feeder- and user-links (MADDPG); bandwidth allocation is non-learned (pp. 6-8).
system: LEO satellite relay (540 km), 20x25 UPA, 8 uplink/8 downlink beams, 49 cells, one GS, 19/29 GHz uplink/downlink, shadowed-Rician fading; no RIS (pp. 3, 11-12).
method: Multi-agent DDPG (DE-MADDPG), one actor-critic agent per beam, epsilon-greedy beam selection, state/reward decomposition, non-cooperation penalty; reinforcement learning, offline training (pp. 8-11).
data_channel: Own Python simulator: free-space path loss, shadowed-Rician fading (Omega 0.835, b0 0.126, m 10.01), ITU-R S.1528 beam pattern, Poisson traffic; parameters from Starlink and 3GPP [48] (pp. 3, 12).
test_conditions: Offline training, 1500 episodes of 1000 slots; evaluated over weight alpha, total traffic 15-30 Gbps, two traffic-variation scenarios, 4 vs 8 beams; no separate train/test scenario stated (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Non-learned: Random and Greedy beam hopping with equal bandwidth and power. Learned: DeepBeam [8] (beam hopping only, average power) and CoMADRL [16] (common-reward MADRL) (p. 12).
metrics: System throughput (Gbps), service fairness (RCSR gap), constraint satisfaction rate, convergence curves versus episode (pp. 5, 12-13).
complexity: Order O(4N^8+N^2+15N+Iu(576N+24961)+Id(320N+8320)+11), test phase; training complexity reduced over 50% by halving agents; no runtime (pp. 6, 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "follows a shadowed Rician distribution"; p. 12: "mainly based on the Starlink configurations [42], [43], [44], [45], [46] and the 3GPP specifications [48]". Own simulator; [48] supplies parameters only, no 3GPP channel model or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "Table V depicts the performance of different schemes under different traffic distributions"; p. 13: "Fig. 10 presents the training results under identical traffic conditions for a satellite with four uplink and downlink and a satellite with eight uplink and downlink beams". The paper never states that a policy trained on one traffic distribution or beam count is applied to another; the 4- and 8-beam runs are separate trainings.
q3_support: p. 12: "Cooperative MADRL (CoMADRL) [16]: All agents use the same reward under the MADRL framework"; p. 12: "Random Beam Hopping Scheme (Random)"; p. 13: "compared with the Random and Greedy schemes, the proposed scheme can boost system throughput by a minimum of 228%"; p. 1: "improves the system performance by up to 57.7% compared to sota MADRL methods".
q4_support: p. 11: "the complexity of the DE-MADDPG algorithm is given by O(Iu (576N + 24961) + Id (320N + 8320))"; the overall order including the GWFPP and interior-point steps follows on p. 11.
q5_support: p. 12: "Simulations are conducted based on the Python 3.7 platform". Own simulator; no link to code or data anywhere in the paper; the Starlink and 3GPP documents supply parameters only.
notes: Title and DOI match on p. 1. Area 6: the learned part sets beam hopping and power in a LEO satellite link (physical-layer control under the satellite clause); bandwidth allocation is solved with GWFPP and the simplex method, not learned (pp. 6-7). q1 borderline: TS 38.811 [48] is cited only for parameters (p. 12) and the channel is an own free-space plus shadowed-Rician model; reviewer to confirm. q2 borderline: Sec. VI-B3 claims generalization over traffic distributions (Table V) without stating a train/test mismatch; reviewer to confirm. q3: CoMADRL [16] and DeepBeam [8] are cited earlier works but are described relative to the proposed method (common reward, average power), so check that they are not ablations.
